Risk statement (cause, event, consequenc: If employee access is not removed promptly after termination, former employees may retain access to business applications, potentially exposing confidential customer and employee information.
Affected asset / process: Business applications; HR and customer data
Threat / cause: Informal HR-to-IT handoff; no tracking of account disablement
Planned action: Link HR termination ticket to IT disablement task with SLA; weekly reconciliation of leaver list to active accounts

Risk title: Backups cannot be restored when needed
Risk statement (cause, event, consequenc: If backups are not tested, the company may be unable to restore order and finance data after an outage or ransomware event, causing prolonged downtime and data loss.
Existing controls: Daily backup jobs with failure alerts
Planned action: Perform and document restoration tests; add semi-annual test to compliance calendar

Risk title: Payroll vendor receives more employee data than necessary
Risk statement (cause, event, consequenc: If the payroll provider is sent data fields not required for payroll, a vendor breach or misuse could expose more employee personal information than necessary.
Threat / cause: Payroll export includes all HR fields
Planned action: Minimise payroll feed fields; add breach-notification timeframe to DPA

Risk statement (cause, event, consequenc: If privileged access reviews are not signed off and exceptions resolved, unnecessary or inappropriate administrator access may persist unnoticed.
Threat / cause: No reviewer sign-off step or reminder
Planned action: Add reviewer sign-off and reminder workflow; resolve 4 flagged accounts

Risk statement (cause, event, consequenc: If staff do not know how or how quickly to report suspected incidents, response may be delayed, increasing damage and delaying any required notifications.
Planned action: Define reporting timeframe and out-of-hours contact; approve procedure v2.0; brief all staff

Risk statement (cause, event, consequenc: If staff fall for phishing emails, attackers may gain access to email or business systems, potentially leading to data theft or fraudulent orders.
Existing controls: Email filtering; annual awareness training; MFA on admin and remote access
Planned action: Raise training completion to 95% or more; add quarterly phishing simulations

Risk statement (cause, event, consequenc: If cloud storage permissions are misconfigured, business documents and order exports could be exposed to unauthorised parties.
Threat / cause: Complex sharing settings; no periodic configuration review
Planned action: Quarterly storage configuration review; alert on public links

Risk statement (cause, event, consequenc: If BrightCart does not confirm which PCI DSS requirements apply to its checkout, it may miss obligations to its payment processor or store card data unintentionally.
Threat / cause: Reliance on processor without confirming validation type
Existing controls: Hosted payment page via PayGate; no card data stored (to be verified)
Planned action: Confirm scope and validation type with qualified guidance; retain processor attestation annually

Risk statement (cause, event, consequenc: If security updates are not applied on time, attackers may exploit known weaknesses in servers or applications, leading to unauthorised access.
Threat / cause: Patching is ad hoc; no tracking
Planned action: Define patch timeframes; produce monthly patch report

Risk statement (cause, event, consequenc: If office internet fails, staff in the office may lose connectivity for short periods; staff can use mobile hotspots and cloud tools.
Planned action: Risk accepted by Operations Manager; revisit if outages exceed 4 hours per year
